-/-! ## Part I: Abstract Transport Principle
-
-The key insight: if we have
-- a class of protocols with a tropical cost measure,
-- a class of branching programs with a size/depth measure,
-- a simulation from BPs to protocols with bounded overhead,
-- a certified lower bound on protocol cost,
-
-then the lower bound transfers to branching programs by simple arithmetic.
-This is model-independent and reusable.
--/
-
-namespace TropicalTransfer
-
-/-!
-### Core Transport Theorem (Depth Version)
-
-This is the main abstract transfer lemma. It takes:
-- Protocol and BP as abstract types
-- tropCost: cost measure on protocols (in ℝ, modeling tropical path cost)
-- bpDepth: depth measure on branching programs
-- simulate: maps each BP to a protocol
-- L: certified lower bound on protocol cost
-- C: simulation overhead constant
-
-The theorem is purely arithmetic once the interface axioms are given.
--/
-
-/-
-**Tropical Communication Lower Bound implies Branching Program Depth Lower Bound.**
-
-If every protocol computing f has tropical cost ≥ L, and every branching
-program simulates to a computing protocol with cost ≤ C · depth(BP),
-then every computing branching program has depth ≥ L / C.
-
-This is the core transport principle: tropical hardness migrates across
-model boundaries.
--/
-theorem tropical_comm_lb_implies_bp_depth_lb
-    {Protocol BP : Type}
-    (tropCost : Protocol → ℝ)
-    (bpDepth : BP → ℕ)
-    (simulate : BP → Protocol)
-    (computesP : Protocol → Prop)
-    (computesB : BP → Prop)
-    (L C : ℝ)
-    (hC : 0 < C)
-    (hsim : ∀ B, computesB B → tropCost (simulate B) ≤ C * (bpDepth B : ℝ))
-    (hLB : ∀ prot, computesP prot → L ≤ tropCost prot)
-    (hcomp : ∀ B, computesB B → computesP (simulate B)) :
-    ∀ B, computesB B → L / C ≤ (bpDepth B : ℝ) := by
-  exact fun B hB => by rw [ div_le_iff₀' hC ] ; exact le_trans ( hLB _ ( hcomp _ hB ) ) ( hsim _ hB ) ;
-
-/-
-**Tropical Communication Lower Bound implies Branching Program Size Lower Bound.**
-
-Variant of the transport principle for node-count (size) rather than depth.
-The simulation overhead relates tropical cost to log of size.
--/
-theorem tropical_comm_lb_implies_bp_size_lb
-    {Protocol BP : Type}
-    (tropCost : Protocol → ℝ)
-    (bpSize : BP → ℕ)
-    (simulate : BP → Protocol)
-    (computesP : Protocol → Prop)
-    (computesB : BP → Prop)
-    (L C : ℝ)
-    (hC : 0 < C)
-    (hsim : ∀ B, computesB B → tropCost (simulate B) ≤ C * (bpSize B : ℝ))
-    (hLB : ∀ prot, computesP prot → L ≤ tropCost prot)
-    (hcomp : ∀ B, computesB B → computesP (simulate B)) :
-    ∀ B, computesB B → L / C ≤ (bpSize B : ℝ) := by
-  exact fun B hB => by rw [ div_le_iff₀' hC ] ; linarith [ hLB _ ( hcomp B hB ), hsim B hB ] ;
-
-/-!
-### Direct-Sum Transport Corollary
-
-If tropical costs add under function composition/product, then
-branching program depth lower bounds add as well.
--/
-
-/-
-**Direct-sum branching program lower bound from tropical additivity.**
-
-When tropical communication lower bounds are additive under product
-composition (L₁ + L₂ ≤ tropCost of the product protocol), branching
-program depth lower bounds inherit the same additivity.
--/
-theorem bp_depth_direct_sum_lb
-    {Protocol BP : Type}
-    (tropCost : Protocol → ℝ)
-    (bpDepth : BP → ℕ)
-    (simulate : BP → Protocol)
-    (computesP : Protocol → Prop)
-    (computesB : BP → Prop)
-    (L₁ L₂ C : ℝ)
-    (hC : 0 < C)
-    (hsim : ∀ B, computesB B → tropCost (simulate B) ≤ C * (bpDepth B : ℝ))
-    (hLB : ∀ prot, computesP prot → L₁ + L₂ ≤ tropCost prot)
-    (hcomp : ∀ B, computesB B → computesP (simulate B)) :
-    ∀ B, computesB B → (L₁ + L₂) / C ≤ (bpDepth B : ℝ) := by
-  exact fun B hB => by rw [ div_le_iff₀' hC ] ; exact le_trans ( hLB _ ( hcomp _ hB ) ) ( hsim _ hB ) ;
-
-/-!
-### Concrete Instantiation: AND-like Functions
-
-Use the tropical_and_bound (min a b ≤ a) principle to derive a concrete
-lower bound for AND-like Boolean functions.
--/
-
-/-
-**AND function branching program depth lower bound.**
-
-For AND-like functions where each input variable contributes
-tropical cost ≥ 1, the branching program must have depth ≥ n/C
-where n is the number of variables.
--/
-theorem and_function_bp_depth_lb
-    {Protocol BP : Type}
-    (tropCost : Protocol → ℝ)
-    (bpDepth : BP → ℕ)
-    (simulate : BP → Protocol)
-    (computesP : Protocol → Prop)
-    (computesB : BP → Prop)
-    (n : ℕ)
-    (C : ℝ)
-    (hC : 0 < C)
-    (hsim : ∀ B, computesB B → tropCost (simulate B) ≤ C * (bpDepth B : ℝ))
-    (hLB : ∀ prot, computesP prot → (n : ℝ) ≤ tropCost prot)
-    (hcomp : ∀ B, computesB B → computesP (simulate B)) :
-    ∀ B, computesB B → (n : ℝ) / C ≤ (bpDepth B : ℝ) := by
-  exact fun B hB => by rw [ div_le_iff₀' hC ] ; linarith [ hsim B hB, hLB _ ( hcomp B hB ) ] ;
-
-/-
-**Product composition branching program lower bound.**
-
-If f and g independently require tropical costs L_f and L_g,
-the product f × g requires branching program depth at least (L_f + L_g) / C.
--/
-theorem product_bp_depth_lb
-    {Protocol BP : Type}
-    (tropCost : Protocol → ℝ)
-    (bpDepth : BP → ℕ)
-    (simulate : BP → Protocol)
-    (computesP : Protocol → Prop)
-    (computesB : BP → Prop)
-    (Lf Lg C : ℝ)
-    (hC : 0 < C)
-    (_hLf : 0 ≤ Lf) (_hLg : 0 ≤ Lg)
-    (hsim : ∀ B, computesB B → tropCost (simulate B) ≤ C * (bpDepth B : ℝ))
-    (hLB : ∀ prot, computesP prot → Lf + Lg ≤ tropCost prot)
-    (hcomp : ∀ B, computesB B → computesP (simulate B)) :
-    ∀ B, computesB B → (Lf + Lg) / C ≤ (bpDepth B : ℝ) := by
-  exact fun B hB => by rw [ div_le_iff₀' hC ] ; linarith [ hsim B hB, hLB _ ( hcomp B hB ) ] ;
-
-end TropicalTransfer
-
-/-! ## Part II: Spectral–Tropical Cycle Bridge
-
-We work with finite weighted directed graphs represented as matrices.
-The key transform: a stochastic matrix P becomes a tropical weight
-matrix W via W(i,j) = -log P(i,j).
-
-Spectral expansion (bounded entries, positive gap) forces tropical
-cycle separation (positive cycle gap).
--/
-
-namespace SpectralTropicalCycleBridge
-
-variable {n : ℕ}
-
-/-- Row-stochastic matrix predicate. -/
-def RowStochastic (P : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ) : Prop :=
-  ∀ i, ∑ j, P i j = 1
-
-/-- Strictly positive matrix predicate. -/
-def PositiveMatrix (P : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ) : Prop :=
-  ∀ i j, 0 < P i j
-
-/-- Log-weight transform: converts stochastic matrix to tropical weights. -/
-def logWeight (P : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ) : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ :=
-  fun i j => -Real.log (P i j)
-
-/-- Triangle mean weight for cycle i → j → k → i. -/
-def triangleMean (W : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ) (i j k : Fin n) : ℝ :=
-  (W i j + W j k + W k i) / 3
-
-/-- Maximum entry of a matrix on Fin (n+1). -/
-def maxEntry (P : Fin (n + 1) → Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) : ℝ :=
-  Finset.sup' Finset.univ ⟨0, Finset.mem_univ 0⟩
-    (fun i => Finset.sup' Finset.univ ⟨0, Finset.mem_univ 0⟩ (fun j => P i j))
-
-/-- Spectral gap surrogate: 1 - max entry. Positive when no entry dominates. -/
-def spectralGapSurrogate (P : Fin (n + 1) → Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) : ℝ :=
-  1 - maxEntry P
-
-/-- Triangle cycle gap: minimum triangle mean over all triples. -/
-def triangleCycleGap (W : Fin (n + 1) → Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) : ℝ :=
-  Finset.inf' Finset.univ ⟨0, Finset.mem_univ 0⟩
-    (fun i => Finset.inf' Finset.univ ⟨0, Finset.mem_univ 0⟩
-      (fun j => Finset.inf' Finset.univ ⟨0, Finset.mem_univ 0⟩
-        (fun k => triangleMean W i j k)))
-
-/-- Antitone property of -log on positive reals. -/
-theorem neg_log_antitone {x s : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (_hs : 0 < s) (hxs : x ≤ s) :
-    -Real.log s ≤ -Real.log x := by
-  linarith [Real.log_le_log hx hxs]
-
-/-- Positivity of -log(1-ε) when 0 < ε < 1. -/
-theorem neg_log_one_sub_pos {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
-    0 < -Real.log (1 - ε) :=
-  neg_pos_of_neg (Real.log_neg (by linarith) (by linarith))
-
-/-
-Triangle mean of log-weights is bounded below by -log(max entry).
--/
-theorem triangleMean_logWeight_lb
-    (P : Fin (n + 1) → Fin (n + 1) → ℝ)
-    {s : ℝ} (hpos : PositiveMatrix P) (hs : 0 < s)
-    (hbound : ∀ i j, P i j ≤ s) (i j k : Fin (n + 1)) :
-    -Real.log s ≤ triangleMean (logWeight P) i j k := by
-  unfold triangleMean logWeight;
-  linarith [ neg_log_antitone ( hpos i j ) hs ( hbound i j ), neg_log_antitone ( hpos j k ) hs ( hbound j k ), neg_log_antitone ( hpos k i ) hs ( hbound k i ) ]
-
-/-
-Triangle cycle gap is bounded below by -log(max entry).
--/
-theorem triangleCycleGap_lb
-    (P : Fin (n + 1) → Fin (n + 1) → ℝ)
-    {s : ℝ} (hpos : PositiveMatrix P) (hs : 0 < s)
-    (hbound : ∀ i j, P i j ≤ s) :
-    -Real.log s ≤ triangleCycleGap (logWeight P) := by
-  apply Finset.le_inf';
-  exact fun i _ => Finset.le_inf' _ _ fun j _ => Finset.le_inf' _ _ fun k _ => triangleMean_logWeight_lb P hpos hs hbound i j k
-
-/-
-**Core Bridge: Uniform non-determinism forces positive tropical cycle gap.**
-
-If all entries of a positive matrix P satisfy P(i,j) ≤ 1 - ε with 0 < ε < 1,
-then the tropical triangle cycle gap is positive. This is the fundamental
-connection: classical non-determinism ⟹ tropical cycle separation.
--/
-theorem non_determinism_forces_tropical_gap
-    (P : Fin (n + 1) → Fin (n + 1) → ℝ)
-    (ε : ℝ) (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1)
-    (hpos : PositiveMatrix P)
-    (hbound : ∀ i j, P i j ≤ 1 - ε) :
-    0 < triangleCycleGap (logWeight P) := by
-  exact lt_of_lt_of_le ( by exact neg_log_one_sub_pos hε0 hε1 ) ( triangleCycleGap_lb P hpos ( sub_pos.mpr hε1 ) hbound )
-
-/-
-**Spectral Gap Forces Tropical Cycle Gap.**
-
-When all entries of a positive matrix are strictly less than 1
-(which is forced by row-stochasticity on ≥ 2 states),
-the tropical triangle cycle gap is positive.
-
-This is the main spectral-to-tropical bridge: spectral expansion
-(no deterministic transitions) creates tropical cycle separation.
--/
-theorem spectral_gap_forces_tropical_cycle_gap
-    (P : Fin (n + 1) → Fin (n + 1) → ℝ)
-    (hpos : PositiveMatrix P)
-    (hmax : ∀ i j, P i j < 1) :
-    0 < triangleCycleGap (logWeight P) := by
-  -- Since there are only finitely many entries, there exists some ε > 0 such that all entries are ≤ 1 - ε.
-  obtain ⟨ε, hε⟩ : ∃ ε > 0, ∀ i j, P i j ≤ 1 - ε := by
-    -- Since there are only finitely many entries, there exists a minimum value of $1 - P i j$ over all $i$ and $j$.
-    obtain ⟨ε, hε⟩ : ∃ ε ∈ Set.image (fun (p : Fin (n + 1) × Fin (n + 1)) => 1 - P p.1 p.2) (Set.univ : Set (Fin (n + 1) × Fin (n + 1))), ∀ x ∈ Set.image (fun (p : Fin (n + 1) × Fin (n + 1)) => 1 - P p.1 p.2) (Set.univ : Set (Fin (n + 1) × Fin (n + 1))), ε ≤ x := by
-      exact ⟨ Finset.min' ( Set.toFinset ( Set.image ( fun p : Fin ( n + 1 ) × Fin ( n + 1 ) => 1 - P p.1 p.2 ) Set.univ ) ) ⟨ _, Set.mem_toFinset.mpr <| Set.mem_image_of_mem _ <| Set.mem_univ ( 0, 0 ) ⟩, Set.mem_toFinset.mp <| Finset.min'_mem _ _, fun x hx => Finset.min'_le _ _ <| Set.mem_toFinset.mpr hx ⟩;
-    exact ⟨ ε, by obtain ⟨ p, _, rfl ⟩ := hε.1; exact sub_pos.mpr ( hmax _ _ ), fun i j => by linarith [ hε.2 _ ( Set.mem_image_of_mem _ ( Set.mem_univ ( i, j ) ) ) ] ⟩;
-  apply non_determinism_forces_tropical_gap;
-  exacts [ hε.1, by linarith [ hpos 0 0, hmax 0 0, hε.2 0 0 ], hpos, hε.2 ]
-
-/-
-Row-stochastic positive matrices on ≥ 2 states have entries < 1.
--/
-theorem rowStochastic_entry_lt_one
-    {m : ℕ} (P : Fin (m + 2) → Fin (m + 2) → ℝ)
-    (hrow : RowStochastic P) (hpos : PositiveMatrix P) :
-    ∀ i j, P i j < 1 := by
-  intro i j; have := hrow i; rw [ ← this ] ; rw [ Finset.sum_eq_add_sum_diff_singleton ( Finset.mem_univ j ) ] ;
-  exact lt_add_of_pos_right _ ( Finset.sum_pos ( fun x hx => hpos i x ) <| Finset.card_pos.mp <| by simp +decide [ Finset.card_sdiff ] )
-
-/-- **Corollary: Row-stochastic positive matrices have positive tropical gap.**
-
-For any row-stochastic strictly positive matrix on ≥ 2 states,
-the tropical triangle cycle gap is automatically positive. This gives
-a clean categorical statement: stochastic mixing ⟹ tropical separation. -/
-theorem rowStochastic_positive_tropical_gap
-    {m : ℕ} (P : Fin (m + 2) → Fin (m + 2) → ℝ)
-    (hrow : RowStochastic P) (hpos : PositiveMatrix P) :
-    0 < triangleCycleGap (logWeight P) :=
-  spectral_gap_forces_tropical_cycle_gap P hpos (rowStochastic_entry_lt_one P hrow hpos)
-
-/-!
-### Converse Direction: Tropical Cycle Gap Constrains Spectral Gap
-
-A small tropical cycle gap means some cycle has small mean weight,
-which means corresponding transition probabilities are close to 1,
-bounding the spectral gap from above.
--/
-
-/-
-**Tropical Cycle Gap Bounds Spectral Gap (2×2 case).**
-
-For a 2×2 positive matrix, if the tropical diagonal mean is small,
-the diagonal entries are close to 1, constraining the spectral gap.
-This is the explicit 2×2 bridge.
--/
-theorem tropical_to_spectral_2x2
-    (P : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → ℝ)
-    (hpos : PositiveMatrix P)
-    (δ : ℝ) (_hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
-    (hdiag : -Real.log (P 0 0) ≤ δ) :
-    Real.exp (-δ) ≤ P 0 0 := by
-  rw [ ← Real.le_log_iff_exp_le ( hpos 0 0 ) ] ; linarith
-
-/-!
-### Spectral-Tropical Sandwich Inequality
-
-Combining both directions, we get a two-sided relationship:
-the spectral gap and tropical cycle gap are mutually constraining.
--/
-
-/-
-**Spectral-Tropical Sandwich (qualitative).**
-
-For a row-stochastic positive matrix on ≥ 2 states:
-- Positive spectral gap ⟹ positive tropical cycle gap (forward bridge)
-- The tropical gap is controlled by -log(1 - spectral gap surrogate)
-
-This creates a certified dictionary between spectral and tropical invariants.
--/
-theorem spectral_tropical_sandwich
-    {m : ℕ} (P : Fin (m + 2) → Fin (m + 2) → ℝ)
-    (_hrow : RowStochastic P) (hpos : PositiveMatrix P)
-    (ε : ℝ) (_hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1)
-    (hbound : ∀ i j, P i j ≤ 1 - ε) :
-    -Real.log (1 - ε) ≤ triangleCycleGap (logWeight P) := by
-  -- Apply the triangleCycleGap_lb lemma with s = 1 - ε.
-  apply triangleCycleGap_lb P (by
-  assumption) (by
-  grind) hbound
-
-end SpectralTropicalCycleBridge
-
-/-! ## Part III: Unified Bridge Theorem
-
-The composition of Parts I and II: spectral expansion on a graph
-forces tropical cycle separation, which forces protocol cost lower bounds,
-which force branching program lower bounds. -/
-
-namespace UnifiedBridge
-
-/-- **Unified Transport: Spectral Expansion → BP Lower Bounds.**
-
-The full pipeline: given a graph with spectral expansion and a correspondence
-between its cycle structure and a communication problem, branching programs
-for that problem require large depth.
-
-This composes the spectral-tropical bridge with the tropical-BP transport. -/
-theorem spectral_expansion_implies_bp_lb
-    {Protocol BP : Type}
-    (tropCost : Protocol → ℝ)
-    (bpDepth : BP → ℕ)
-    (simulate : BP → Protocol)
-    (computesP : Protocol → Prop)
-    (computesB : BP → Prop)
-    (L C : ℝ)
-    (hC : 0 < C)
-    (_hL : 0 < L)
-    (hsim : ∀ B, computesB B → tropCost (simulate B) ≤ C * (bpDepth B : ℝ))
-    (hLB : ∀ prot, computesP prot → L ≤ tropCost prot)
-    (hcomp : ∀ B, computesB B → computesP (simulate B)) :
-    ∀ B, computesB B → L / C ≤ (bpDepth B : ℝ) :=
-  TropicalTransfer.tropical_comm_lb_implies_bp_depth_lb
-    tropCost bpDepth simulate computesP computesB L C hC hsim hLB hcomp
-
-end UnifiedBridge

+namespace Tropical
+
+variable (V : Type*) [Fintype V]
+
+/-- A `ComplexityTransfer` bundles a tropical graph on the finite vertex type `V`
+(`weight`, a min-plus weight matrix) with a row-stochastic transition matrix `P`,
+transferring the combinatorial data to the finite-dimensional real vector space
+`V → ℝ`. -/
+structure ComplexityTransfer where
+  /-- Min-plus edge weights of the tropical graph. -/
+  weight : Matrix V V (Tropical ℝ)
+  /-- Real transition matrix attached to the graph. -/
+  P : Matrix V V ℝ
+  /-- The transition matrix has nonnegative entries. -/
+  P_nonneg : ∀ i j, 0 ≤ P i j
+  /-- Each row of the transition matrix sums to one (row-stochastic). -/
+  P_rowSum : ∀ i, ∑ j, P i j = 1
+
+namespace ComplexityTransfer
+
+variable {V}
+
+/-! ### The transfer space and module compatibility -/
+
+/-- The finite-dimensional real transfer space attached to the vertex set. -/
+abbrev transferSpace (_C : ComplexityTransfer V) : Type _ := V → ℝ
+
+/-- The transfer space `V → ℝ` is finite-dimensional, of dimension `card V`. -/
+theorem transferSpace_finrank : Module.finrank ℝ (V → ℝ) = Fintype.card V :=
+  Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card ℝ
+
+/-- The transfer endomorphism of `V → ℝ` induced by the transition matrix:
+an honest `ℝ`-linear map (module compatibility). -/
+noncomputable def transferMap (C : ComplexityTransfer V) : (V → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] (V → ℝ) :=
+  Matrix.mulVecLin C.P
+
+@[simp] theorem transferMap_apply (C : ComplexityTransfer V) (w : V → ℝ) :
+    C.transferMap w = C.P.mulVec w :=
+  Matrix.mulVecLin_apply C.P w
+
+theorem transferMap_add (C : ComplexityTransfer V) (w₁ w₂ : V → ℝ) :
+    C.transferMap (w₁ + w₂) = C.transferMap w₁ + C.transferMap w₂ :=
+  map_add C.transferMap w₁ w₂
+
+theorem transferMap_smul (C : ComplexityTransfer V) (a : ℝ) (w : V → ℝ) :
+    C.transferMap (a • w) = a • C.transferMap w :=
+  map_smul C.transferMap a w
+
+/-! ### Stochastic stationarity -/
+
+/-- The all-ones vector is fixed by the transition matrix: `1` is an eigenvalue. -/
+theorem mulVec_const_one (C : ComplexityTransfer V) :
+    C.P.mulVec (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) = (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) := by
+  funext i; simp [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, C.P_rowSum i]
+
+/-- The probability simplex is invariant under the left (`vecMul`) action of a
+row-stochastic matrix: if `w` is a probability vector then so is `w ᵥ* P`. -/
+theorem vecMul_isProb (C : ComplexityTransfer V) (w : V → ℝ)
+    (hw_nonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (hw_sum : ∑ i, w i = 1) :
+    (∀ j, 0 ≤ (Matrix.vecMul w C.P) j) ∧ (∑ j, (Matrix.vecMul w C.P) j = 1) := by
+  refine ⟨fun j => Finset.sum_nonneg (fun i _ => mul_nonneg (hw_nonneg i) (C.P_nonneg i j)), ?_⟩
+  simp only [Matrix.vecMul, dotProduct]
+  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+  simp_rw [← Finset.mul_sum, C.P_rowSum, mul_one]
+  exact hw_sum
+
+/-! ### Oscillation and Doeblin convergence -/
+
+section Convergence
+
+variable [Nonempty V]
+
+/-- The oscillation (range) of a real vector on the finite vertex set. -/
+noncomputable def osc (w : V → ℝ) : ℝ :=
+  (Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty w) - (Finset.univ.inf' Finset.univ_nonempty w)
+
+theorem osc_nonneg (w : V → ℝ) : 0 ≤ osc w := by
+  obtain ⟨i, _⟩ := (Finset.univ_nonempty (α := V))
+  exact sub_nonneg.mpr
+    (le_trans (Finset.inf'_le _ (mem_univ i)) (Finset.le_sup' _ (mem_univ i)))
+
+variable (C : ComplexityTransfer V) {δ : ℝ}
+
+/-- Under a uniform lower bound `δ ≤ P i j` the total mass forces `(card V) * δ ≤ 1`. -/
+theorem card_mul_delta_le_one (hδ : ∀ i j, δ ≤ C.P i j) :
+    (Fintype.card V : ℝ) * δ ≤ 1 := by
+  obtain ⟨i, _⟩ := (Finset.univ_nonempty (α := V))
+  have h : (Fintype.card V : ℝ) * δ = ∑ _j : V, δ := by
+    rw [Finset.sum_const]; simp [Finset.card_univ]
+  rw [h, ← C.P_rowSum i]
+  exact Finset.sum_le_sum (fun j _ => hδ i j)
+
+/-- **One-step Doeblin contraction of oscillation.**  If every entry of `P` is at least
+`δ`, then a single application of `P` contracts the oscillation by the factor
+`ρ = 1 - (card V) * δ`. -/
+theorem osc_mulVec_le (hδ : ∀ i j, δ ≤ C.P i j) (w : V → ℝ) :
+    osc (C.P.mulVec w) ≤ (1 - (Fintype.card V : ℝ) * δ) * osc w := by
+  -- It suffices to bound, for every pair of vertices `i k`, the gap of the new vector.
+  have h_osc_le : ∀ i k, (C.P *ᵥ w) i - (C.P *ᵥ w) k ≤ (1 - Fintype.card V * δ) * osc w := by
+    intro i k
+    have h_osc_sum :
+        ∑ j, (C.P i j - C.P k j) * (w j - (Finset.univ.inf' Finset.univ_nonempty w)) ≤
+          ∑ j, (C.P i j - δ) *
+            ((Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty w) -
+              (Finset.univ.inf' Finset.univ_nonempty w)) := by
+      refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun j _ => ?_
+      nlinarith [hδ i j, hδ k j,
+        show w j ≤ Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty w from
+          Finset.le_sup' (fun x => w x) (Finset.mem_univ j),
+        show Finset.univ.inf' Finset.univ_nonempty w ≤ w j from
+          Finset.inf'_le _ (Finset.mem_univ j)]
+    simp_all +decide [mul_sub, sub_mul, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, osc]
+    simp_all +decide [← mul_assoc, ← Finset.sum_mul _ _ _, C.P_rowSum]
+    convert h_osc_sum using 1
+  refine sub_le_iff_le_add'.mpr ?_
+  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup' Finset.univ_nonempty (fun i => (C.P *ᵥ w) i)
+  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_inf' Finset.univ_nonempty (fun i => (C.P *ᵥ w) i)
+  linarith [h_osc_le i k]
+
+section Powers
+
+variable [DecidableEq V]
+
+/-- **Geometric decay of oscillation along the powers of `P`.** -/
+theorem osc_pow_mulVec_le (hδ : ∀ i j, δ ≤ C.P i j) (w : V → ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
+    osc ((C.P ^ n).mulVec w) ≤ (1 - (Fintype.card V : ℝ) * δ) ^ n * osc w := by
+  induction n with
+  | zero => simp
+  | succ n ih =>
+    have h_step :
+        osc (C.P.mulVec ((C.P ^ n) *ᵥ w)) ≤
+          (1 - (Fintype.card V : ℝ) * δ) * osc ((C.P ^ n) *ᵥ w) := osc_mulVec_le C hδ _
+    have hρ : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 1 - (Fintype.card V : ℝ) * δ :=
+      sub_nonneg_of_le (by simpa using card_mul_delta_le_one C hδ)
+    calc osc ((C.P ^ (n + 1)).mulVec w)
+        = osc (C.P.mulVec ((C.P ^ n) *ᵥ w)) := by rw [pow_succ', Matrix.mulVec_mulVec]
+      _ ≤ (1 - (Fintype.card V : ℝ) * δ) * osc ((C.P ^ n) *ᵥ w) := h_step
+      _ ≤ (1 - (Fintype.card V : ℝ) * δ) *
+            ((1 - (Fintype.card V : ℝ) * δ) ^ n * osc w) :=
+          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ih hρ
+      _ = (1 - (Fintype.card V : ℝ) * δ) ^ (n + 1) * osc w := by ring
+
+/-- **Stochastic convergence.** Under a uniform positive lower bound on the entries of
+the transition matrix, the oscillation of `Pⁿ ·ᵥ w` tends to `0`: the Markov dynamics
+forgets its initial condition. -/
+theorem tendsto_osc_pow_mulVec (hδpos : 0 < δ) (hδ : ∀ i j, δ ≤ C.P i j) (w : V → ℝ) :
+    Tendsto (fun n => osc ((C.P ^ n).mulVec w)) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
+  refine squeeze_zero (fun n => osc_nonneg _) (fun n => osc_pow_mulVec_le C hδ w n) ?_
+  have hρ : Tendsto (fun n => (1 - (Fintype.card V : ℝ) * δ) ^ n) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
+    tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one
+      (sub_nonneg.2 (card_mul_delta_le_one C hδ))
+      (sub_lt_self _ (mul_pos (Nat.cast_pos.2 Fintype.card_pos) hδpos))
+  simpa using hρ.mul_const (osc w)
+
+end Powers
+
+end Convergence
+
+end ComplexityTransfer
+
+end Tropical

# Computational Evidence — Sheaf-Theoretic Data Integration

Concise numerical sanity checks supporting the formal theorems in
`Applications/SheafDataIntegration/`. All claims below are *proved* in Lean; this
file only records the small-case evidence that guided the formalization.

## 1. Counting law `#completions = qᵐ`

Setup: value alphabet `α` with `q = #α`; a database over rows `R`; `m =
missingCells D R` is the number of missing cells in the rows of `R`.

`card_dataSection_eq : Fintype.card (DataSection D R) = q ^ m`.

Hand-computed instances (each cell is `Option α`, `•` = observed, `?` = missing):

| database (rows in R) | q | m | predicted `qᵐ` | direct count |
|----------------------|---|---|----------------|--------------|
| `[• •]`              | 2 | 0 | `2^0 = 1`      | 1 (only itself) |
| `[• ?]`              | 2 | 1 | `2^1 = 2`      | 2 (`? ∈ {0,1}`) |
| `[? ?]`              | 2 | 2 | `2^2 = 4`      | 4 |
| `[? ?]`              | 3 | 2 | `3^2 = 9`      | 9 |
| `[• ?; ? •]` (2 rows)| 2 | 2 | `2^2 = 4`      | 4 |

All match. The exponent `m` is a sum over rows (`missingCells` is a `Finset.sum`),
so it is automatically additive over disjoint row blocks — see §3.

## 2. Corollaries cross-checked

* `unique_completion_of_fullyObserved`: `m = 0 ⇒ qᵐ = 1` ✓ (row `[• •]` above).
* `nonunique_completion_of_missing`: `q ≥ 2`, `m ≥ 1 ⇒ qᵐ ≥ 2` ✓ (rows with a `?`).
* `card_dataSection_pos`: `q ≥ 1 ⇒ qᵐ ≥ 1` ✓ (every row above has ≥ 1 completion).

The sequence of completion counts for a single fully-missing row of width `n`
over a binary alphabet is `2^n = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, …` (OEIS A000079, powers of 2);
over a ternary alphabet `3^n = 1, 3, 9, 27, …` (OEIS A000244). These are exactly
`q ^ (#columns)` when every cell is missing, the `m = n` special case.

## 3. Independence across disjoint row blocks

`card_dataSection_union_disjoint`: for `Disjoint R₁ R₂`,
`#completions(R₁ ∪ R₂) = #completions(R₁) · #completions(R₂)`.

Check: `R₁ = [• ?]` (count 2), `R₂ = [? ?]` (count 4), disjoint rows ⇒ combined
count `2 · 4 = 8 = 2^(1+2)` ✓. The exponents add (`missingCells_union_disjoint`),
the counts multiply — the enumerative shadow of the probabilistic `q ^ C` law.

## 4. Merge / integration

`Database.merge D₁ D₂` keeps observed cells of either source (preferring `D₁`).

* `merge_observed_eq`: observed cells of the merge = union of observed cells ✓
  (`[• ?]` merged with `[? •]` ⇒ `[• •]`, fully observed).
* `consistent_merge_iff` (under agreement on overlaps): completions of the merge
  = assignments consistent with *both* sources. Check on `[• ?]` ⊔ `[? •]` = `[• •]`:
  unique completion, and it is the unique common refinement ✓.
* Monotonicity (`card_dataSection_merge_le_left`): merging `[• ?]` (2 completions)
  with `[? •]` yields `[• •]` (1 completion), and `1 ≤ 2` ✓. Integration never
  increases the completion count, because it can only reveal cells.

## 5. Counterexample hunt

* Forward direction of `consistent_merge_iff` **requires** the agreement
  hypothesis: merging `[• = 0]` with `[• = 1]` on the same cell gives merge `= 0`
  (D₁ preferred); the assignment `0` is consistent with the merge but not with D₂.
  Hence the iff fails without `agree` — the hypothesis is load-bearing, not
  decorative. This is why `agree` appears in the statement.
* No counterexample to the counting law was found across all small cases tried;
  it is now proved in full generality.

# Future Directions — Sheaf-Theoretic Data Integration

This cycle established, fully formally (0 sorries, only `propext`,
`Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`):

* **Databases form a sheaf** (`dataSheaf_glue_unique`): compatible local
  completions glue to a *unique* global completion (equalizer/`∃!`).
* **Counting law** (`card_dataSection_eq`): `#completions = q ^ (missing cells)`,
  via an explicit bijection `DataSection ≃ (FreeCell → α)`.
* **Independence across disjoint row blocks** (`card_dataSection_union_disjoint`):
  exponents add, counts multiply.
* **Integration = intersection of section spaces** (`consistent_merge_iff`):
  merging compatible sources intersects their completion spaces; integration is
  monotone (`card_dataSection_merge_le_left`).

The following conjectures are precise and testable targets for the next cycles.

## Conjecture 1 (Inclusion–exclusion for incompatible merges)

When two sources **disagree** on some overlap cells, `consistent_merge_iff`
fails. Conjecture: the number of *jointly* consistent completions is governed by
the agreement locus. Precisely, define `Agree D₁ D₂` = the set of cells where the
sources are both observed and equal. Then the assignments consistent with both
`D₁` and `D₂` are non-empty **iff** the sources agree on every commonly-observed
cell, and in that case their count is `q ^ (cells missing in *both* sources)`.
Testable form: `Nonempty {g // Consistent D₁ R g ∧ Consistent D₂ R g} ↔ (∀ overlap
cells agree)`, and when non-empty its cardinality is `q ^ missingCells (merge) R`.

## Conjecture 2 (Cohomological obstruction to global integration)

Generalize beyond two sources to a cover `{Dₐ}` of partial databases. Conjecture:
a global consistent integration exists **iff** a Čech 1-cocycle assembled from the
pairwise overlap discrepancies is a coboundary, i.e. `H¹ = 0` for the discrepancy
cochain on the overlap nerve. This would connect the `MachineLearning/CechComplex`
machinery (`IsOneCocycle`, `cocycle_eq_coboundary_on_total`) to multi-source
integration, upgrading the pairwise `consistent_merge_iff` to an `n`-source
obstruction theory. Testable: for 3 sources, pairwise compatibility + triangle
cocycle condition ⇒ global section exists.

## Conjecture 3 (Entropy of the completion sheaf)

Under the uniform distribution on completions, the Shannon entropy of the data
sheaf over `R` is exactly `missingCells D R · log q`. Conjecture: entropy is
additive over disjoint row blocks (from `card_dataSection_union_disjoint`) and
*sub*additive under merge: `H(merge D₁ D₂) ≤ min (H D₁) (H D₂)`, with equality iff
the second source observes no new cells. This makes "information gained by
integration" a provable quantity `H(D₁) − H(merge D₁ D₂) = (missing reduction)·log q ≥ 0`.

## Conjecture 4 (Column-wise functional dependencies as a subsheaf)

Restrict the data sheaf to completions satisfying a functional dependency
`X → Y` (rows agreeing on columns `X` must agree on columns `Y`). Conjecture: the
FD-constrained completions form a *subsheaf* (closed under restriction and
gluing), and their count is `q ^ (free cells modulo the FD)` where the exponent
subtracts one degree of freedom per determined cell. Testable: for a single FD on
a 2-row database, the count drops from `q^m` to `q^(m − d)` with `d` the number
of `Y`-cells forced by equal `X`-keys.

## Conjecture 5 (Sheaf of joins / relational algebra)

The natural/inner join of two databases corresponds to a *fibre product* in the
category of data sheaves. Conjecture: `DataSection (join D₁ D₂) ≃` the pullback
`DataSection D₁ ×_{shared} DataSection D₂`, and the counting law specializes to
`#completions(join) = Σ_keys q^(missing in matched rows)`. This would realize the
core relational-algebra operators (select = subsheaf, project = pushforward, join
= pullback) inside the sheaf framework, with `consistent_merge_iff` as the
union/outer-join special case.

# A Finite Dependency Calculus for Theorem Libraries: Anti-Gravity Theorems

This file formalizes a small, fully finite *dependency calculus* for theorem
libraries.  A **finite library** is a finite collection of theorems together
with a direct-dependency relation `depends u t` ("theorem `u` depends directly
on theorem `t`") and a proof-length assignment `proofLen`.

The central notion is that of an **anti-gravity theorem**: a theorem that is
simultaneously *cheap to prove* (small proof length) and *heavily relied upon*
(large in-degree / weight).  Such theorems "defy gravity": despite being light,
they hold up a large part of the library.

## Main definitions

* `FiniteLibrary α` — a finite theorem library on the finite index type `α`.
* `weight L t` — the number of theorems that depend directly on `t` (its
  in-degree in the dependency graph).
* `AntiGravity L K B t` — `t` has weight at least `K` and proof length at most `B`.
* `shortSet L B` — the theorems with proof length at most `B`.
* `antiGravityCandidates L K B` — the executable finset of anti-gravity theorems.
* `Reaches L` — reachability `Relation.ReflTransGen L.depends` (edge `u → t`
  when `u` depends on `t`).
* `DepDense L S` — every theorem reaches some theorem of `S` by dependency steps.

## Main results

* `weight_le_card` — weight is bounded by the size of the library.
* `antigravity_mono` — anti-gravity is monotone: lowering `K` and raising `B`
  preserves it.
* `mem_antiGravityCandidates` / `shortSet_mem` — the executable finsets compute
  the intended predicates.
* `totalWeight_le_of_all_light` — if every short theorem is light
  (`weight < K`), the total short weight is at most `card · (K-1)`.
* `antigravity_pigeonhole` — a pigeonhole converse: enough total short weight
  forces an anti-gravity theorem to exist.
* `DepDense_mono` — dependency density is monotone in the target set.

## The star library

The running example `starLibrary n` is a "star": one center theorem `none`
together with `n` leaves `some i`, each leaf depending directly on the center.
The center is the unique anti-gravity theorem, has weight `n`, and the singleton
`{center}` is dependency-dense.
-/

import Mathlib

open Finset

namespace AntiGravityFinite

/-- A **finite theorem library** on a finite index type `α`.

`depends u t` means theorem `u` depends *directly* on theorem `t`, and
`proofLen t` records the length (cost) of the proof of `t`.  We carry an explicit
decidability witness for `depends` so that all derived finsets are executable. -/
structure FiniteLibrary (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] where
  /-- `depends u t`: theorem `u` depends directly on theorem `t`. -/
  depends : α → α → Prop

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-- The **weight** of a theorem `t` is the number of theorems `u` that depend
directly on `t` — i.e. the in-degree of `t` in the dependency graph. -/
def weight (L : FiniteLibrary α) (t : α) : Nat :=
  (Finset.univ.filter (fun u => L.depends u t)).card

`K` theorems yet has proof length at most `B`. -/
def AntiGravity (L : FiniteLibrary α) (K B : Nat) (t : α) : Prop :=
  K ≤ weight L t ∧ L.proofLen t ≤ B

/-- The finset of **short** theorems: those with proof length at most `B`. -/
def shortSet (L : FiniteLibrary α) (B : Nat) : Finset α :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun t => L.proofLen t ≤ B)

def antiGravityCandidates (L : FiniteLibrary α) (K B : Nat) : Finset α :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun t => K ≤ weight L t ∧ L.proofLen t ≤ B)

def Reaches (L : FiniteLibrary α) : α → α → Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen L.depends

some theorem of `S` in zero or more dependency steps. -/
def DepDense (L : FiniteLibrary α) (S : Finset α) : Prop :=
  ∀ u : α, ∃ t ∈ S, Reaches L u t

length budget `B` preserves the property. -/
theorem antigravity_mono (L : FiniteLibrary α) {K K' B B' : Nat} {t : α}
    (hK : K' ≤ K) (hB : B ≤ B') (h : AntiGravity L K B t) :
    AntiGravity L K' B' t := by
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := h
  exact ⟨le_trans hK h1, le_trans h2 hB⟩

theorem mem_antiGravityCandidates (L : FiniteLibrary α) (K B : Nat) (t : α) :

  unfold antiGravityCandidates AntiGravity
  simp [Finset.mem_filter]

theorem shortSet_mem (L : FiniteLibrary α) (B : Nat) (t : α) :
    t ∈ shortSet L B ↔ L.proofLen t ≤ B := by
  unfold shortSet
  simp [Finset.mem_filter]

/-- If every short theorem is **light** (weight strictly below `K`) and `K` is
positive, then the total weight over short theorems is at most
`(shortSet L B).card * (K - 1)`.  This uses the `Nat` fact that `w < K` together
with `0 < K` gives `w ≤ K - 1`. -/
theorem totalWeight_le_of_all_light (L : FiniteLibrary α) {K B : Nat}
    (hK : 0 < K) (hlight : ∀ t ∈ shortSet L B, weight L t < K) :
    ∑ t ∈ shortSet L B, weight L t ≤ (shortSet L B).card * (K - 1) := by
  calc ∑ t ∈ shortSet L B, weight L t
      ≤ ∑ _t ∈ shortSet L B, (K - 1) := by
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro t ht

        omega

        rw [Finset.sum_const, smul_eq_mul]

theorems exceeds `(shortSet L B).card * (K - 1)`, then some theorem is an

`totalWeight_le_of_all_light`. -/
theorem antigravity_pigeonhole (L : FiniteLibrary α) {K B : Nat}
    (hK : 0 < K)
    (hsum : ∑ t ∈ shortSet L B, weight L t > (shortSet L B).card * (K - 1)) :
    ∃ t, AntiGravity L K B t := by
  by_contra h
  push_neg at h
  have hlight : ∀ t ∈ shortSet L B, weight L t < K := by
    intro t ht
    have hshort : L.proofLen t ≤ B := (shortSet_mem L B t).mp ht
    have hnt := h t
    by_contra hw
    push_neg at hw
    exact hnt ⟨hw, hshort⟩
  have := totalWeight_le_of_all_light L hK hlight
  omega

/-- Dependency density is monotone in the target set. -/
theorem DepDense_mono (L : FiniteLibrary α) {S T : Finset α}
    (hST : S ⊆ T) (h : DepDense L S) : DepDense L T := by
  intro u
  obtain ⟨t, htS, hreach⟩ := h u
  exact ⟨t, hST htS, hreach⟩

/-! ### The star library

The canonical example: one center theorem `none` and `n` leaf theorems
`some i`, each leaf depending directly on the center. -/

/-- The **star library** on `Option (Fin n)`: `none` is the center, `some i` are
the leaves, and the only dependencies are leaf → center.  The center has proof
length `1` and each leaf has proof length `2`. -/
def starLibrary (n : Nat) : FiniteLibrary (Option (Fin n)) where
  depends u t := match u, t with
    | some _, none => True
    | _, _ => False
  decidableDepends := by
    intro u t
    cases u <;> cases t <;> dsimp <;> infer_instance
  proofLen t := match t with
    | none => 1
    | some _ => 2

/-- The center of the star library. -/
def starCenter {n : Nat} : Option (Fin n) := none

/-- The center has weight exactly `n`: all `n` leaves depend on it.

The filtered finset of direct dependents of `none` is exactly the image of
`some`, which has cardinality `Fintype.card (Fin n) = n`. -/
theorem star_weight_center (n : Nat) :
    weight (starLibrary n) starCenter = n := by
  unfold weight starCenter
  have h : (Finset.univ.filter (fun u => (starLibrary n).depends u none))
       = Finset.univ.image (some : Fin n → Option (Fin n)) := by
    ext u
    cases u with
    | none => simp [starLibrary]
    | some i => simp [starLibrary]
  rw [h, Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (Option.some_injective _)]
  simp

/-- Each leaf has weight `0`: nothing depends on a leaf. -/
theorem star_weight_leaf (n : Nat) (i : Fin n) :
    weight (starLibrary n) (some i) = 0 := by
  unfold weight
  rw [Finset.card_eq_zero, Finset.filter_eq_empty_iff]
  intro u _
  cases u <;> simp [starLibrary]

/-- The center is an anti-gravity theorem at thresholds `K = n`, `B = 1`: it is
relied upon by all `n` leaves yet has proof length `1`. -/
theorem star_center_antigravity (n : Nat) :
    AntiGravity (starLibrary n) n 1 starCenter := by
  constructor
  · exact (star_weight_center n).ge
  · show (starLibrary n).proofLen starCenter ≤ 1
    unfold starCenter
    simp [starLibrary]

/-- The singleton `{center}` is dependency-dense: every leaf reaches the center
by one direct dependency step, and the center reaches itself by reflexivity. -/
theorem star_singleton_depDense (n : Nat) :
    DepDense (starLibrary n) {starCenter} := by
  intro u
  refine ⟨starCenter, Finset.mem_singleton_self _, ?_⟩
  unfold Reaches starCenter
  cases u with
  | none => exact Relation.ReflTransGen.refl
  | some i => exact Relation.ReflTransGen.single trivial

/-- The anti-gravity candidate set at thresholds `K = n`, `B = 1` is
dependency-dense, since it contains the center and `{center}` is dense. -/
theorem star_candidates_depDense (n : Nat) :
    DepDense (starLibrary n) (antiGravityCandidates (starLibrary n) n 1) := by
  refine DepDense_mono (starLibrary n) (S := {starCenter}) ?_ (star_singleton_depDense n)
  rw [Finset.singleton_subset_iff, mem_antiGravityCandidates]
  exact star_center_antigravity n

end AntiGravityFinite

  · exact accelCollatzOdd_odd ( show 0 < accelSeq n k from Nat.pos_of_ne_zero fun h => by simp_all +decide [ Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod ] )

  exact Nat.recOn k hn fun k hk => accelCollatzOdd_pos hk

theorem accelSeq_succ (n : ℕ) (k : ℕ) : accelSeq n (k + 1) = accelSeq (accelCollatzOdd n) k := by
  induction k with
  | zero => simp [accelSeq]
  | succ k ih => simp only [accelSeq]; congr 1

end Collatz

def HasGoodReduction {n p : ℕ}

    (Tp : (Fin n → ZMod p) → (Fin n → ZMod p))
    [Fact p.Prime] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin n → ℤ,
    (fun i => ((T x i : ℤ) : ZMod p)) = Tp (fun i => (x i : ZMod p))

def PhaseLockedAt {α : Type*} (f : α → α) (x : α) (m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  0 < m ∧ ∃ mu : ℕ, f^[mu + m] x = f^[mu] x

    is phase locked with a uniform period bound. -/
def ArithmeticPhaseLocking {n : ℕ}
    (T : (Fin n → ℤ) → (Fin n → ℤ))

theorem iterate_reduce_comm

theorem eventuallyPeriodic_of_finite

    exact absurd ( Finset.card_le_card ( show Finset.image ( fun i => f^[i] x ) ( Finset.range ( Fintype.card α + 1 ) ) ⊆ Finset.univ from Finset.subset_univ _ ) ) ( by rw [ Finset.card_image_of_injOn fun i hi j hj hij => le_antisymm ( not_lt.1 fun hi' => h _ _ hi' ( by linarith [ Finset.mem_range.1 hi, Finset.mem_range.1 hj ] ) hij.symm ) ( not_lt.1 fun hj' => h _ _ hj' ( by linarith [ Finset.mem_range.1 hi, Finset.mem_range.1 hj ] ) hij ), Finset.card_range ] ; simp +decide );

/-
**Injectivity on orbit implies pure periodicity.**
    If f is injective on the forward orbit, the orbit is purely periodic.
-/
theorem injective_on_orbit_implies_periodic
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (f : α → α) (x : α)
    (hinj : Set.InjOn f {y | ∃ t : ℕ, f^[t] x = y}) :
    ∃ per : ℕ, 0 < per ∧ f^[per] x = x := by
  -- By eventuallyPeriodic_of_finite, there exist mu, per with f^[mu + per](x) = f^[mu](x).
  obtain ⟨mu, per, h_mu_per⟩ : ∃ mu per : ℕ, mu < Fintype.card α ∧ 0 < per ∧ per ≤ Fintype.card α ∧ f^[mu + per] x = f^[mu] x := by
    exact eventuallyPeriodic_of_finite f x;
  -- By induction on mu, show that f^[per] x = x.
  induction' mu with mu ih;
  · aesop;
  · simp_all +decide [ Nat.succ_add, Function.iterate_succ_apply' ];
    exact ih ( Nat.lt_of_succ_lt h_mu_per.1 ) ( hinj ⟨ _, rfl ⟩ ⟨ _, rfl ⟩ h_mu_per.2.2.2 )

/-
**Bijective maps on finite types have purely periodic orbits.**
-/
theorem periodic_of_bijective_finite
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (f : α → α) (hf : Function.Bijective f) (x : α) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ f^[n] x = x := by
  -- Since f is bijective, it is a permutation of the finite type α.
  have h_perm : ∃ g : Equiv.Perm α, ∀ x, f x = g x := by
    exact ⟨ Equiv.ofBijective f hf, fun x => rfl ⟩;
  obtain ⟨ g, hg ⟩ := h_perm; use orderOf g; simp +decide [ hg, Function.iterate_fixed, orderOf_pos ] ;

/-! ## Theorem 3: 1D Affine Iteration and Phase Locking -/

/-
**1D affine iterate formula.**
    For T(y) = a*y + b, we have T^[t](x) = a^t * x + (Σ_{k<t} a^k) * b.
-/
theorem affine_1d_iterate (a b : ℤ) (t : ℕ) (x : ℤ) :
    (fun y => a * y + b)^[t] x =
      a ^ t * x + (Finset.range t).sum (fun k => a ^ k) * b := by
  induction t <;> simp +decide [ *, pow_succ', Function.iterate_succ_apply', Finset.mul_sum _ _ _, Finset.sum_range_succ' ] ; ring;
  simpa only [ ← Finset.mul_sum _ _ _, ← Finset.sum_mul ] using by ring;

/-
**1D Spectral Torsion Phase Locking.**
    If a^m = 1 and (Σ_{k<m} a^k) * b = 0, then T^m = id.

    For quadratic loss L(w) = (1/2)Aw² + Bw + C, gradient descent gives
    T(w) = (1 - ηA)w - ηB. Setting a = 1 - ηA: if the "propagator" a is a
    root of unity in ℤ (i.e. a ∈ {1,-1}) and the geometric sum vanishes,
    the discrete optimization flow is exactly periodic — a Floquet-type
    periodicity in arithmetic dynamics.
-/
theorem spectral_torsion_1d (a b : ℤ) (m : ℕ) (_hm : 0 < m)
    (ha : a ^ m = 1)
    (hgeom : (Finset.range m).sum (fun k => a ^ k) * b = 0) :
    ∀ x : ℤ, (fun y => a * y + b)^[m] x = x := by
  intro x
  rw [affine_1d_iterate]
  simp [ha, hgeom]

/-! ## Theorem 4: Cross-Domain Modular Phase Locking -/

/-
**1D affine iterate formula over any commutative ring.**
-/
theorem affine_1d_iterate_ring {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (a b : R) (t : ℕ) (x : R) :
    (fun y => a * y + b)^[t] x =
      a ^ t * x + (Finset.range t).sum (fun k => a ^ k) * b := by
  induction t <;> simp_all +decide [ Function.iterate_succ_apply', pow_succ', Finset.sum_range_succ' ];
  simp +decide [ mul_add, add_mul, mul_assoc, Finset.mul_sum _ _ _, Finset.sum_mul ];
  ring

/-
**Cross-domain: spectral torsion modulo primes.**
    If a^m = 1 over ℤ and the geometric condition holds, then for every
    prime p, the reduced 1D affine map mod p has all orbits periodic with
    period dividing m.

    This connects optimization (quadratic loss), spectral algebra
    (roots of unity), and finite-field dynamics (modular periodicity).
-/
theorem spectral_torsion_modp_1d (a b : ℤ) (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m)
    (ha : a ^ m = 1)
    (hgeom : (Finset.range m).sum (fun k => a ^ k) * b = 0)
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (x : ZMod p) :
    (fun y => (a : ZMod p) * y + (b : ZMod p))^[m] x = x := by
  convert spectral_torsion_1d ( a := a ) ( b := b ) m hm ?_ ?_;
  · constructor <;> intro h;
    · convert spectral_torsion_1d a b m hm ?_ ?_;
      · exact ha;
      · exact hgeom;
    · convert congr_arg ( ( ↑ ) : ℤ → ZMod p ) ( h ( x.val : ℤ ) ) using 1;
      · exact Nat.recOn m ( by simp +decide ) fun n ih => by simp +decide [ *, Function.iterate_succ_apply' ] ;
      · cases p <;> aesop;
  · exact ha;
  · grind

# Asymptotic Tightness for PAC-Bayes Bounds on Linear Classifiers

This file proves that under regularity assumptions on the posterior sequence,
the PAC-Bayes complexity term scales as Θ(d/n) for the equal-variance case
and vanishes as n → ∞ for the general case.

## Main Results

- `pac_bayes_equal_var_rate_upper`: O(1/n) rate for equal-variance KL
- `pac_bayes_linear_rate_lower`: Lower bound Ω(d/n)
- `complexity_vanishes`: The complexity term → 0 as n → ∞
- `complexity_linear_in_d`: Complexity is linear in dimension d
-/

import MachineLearning.PACBayes.Defs
import MachineLearning.PACBayes.GaussianKL

open Real BigOperators Finset Filter

noncomputable section

namespace PACBayes

/-! ## Section 1: Equal-Variance Upper Bound -/

/-
Upper bound for equal-variance case: when prior and posterior share
    variance σ (fixed), the complexity KL/n is O(1/n).
    Precisely: ‖w‖²/(2σ²n) ≤ C_norm/(2σ²n).
-/
theorem pac_bayes_equal_var_rate_upper
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (σ : ℝ) (hσ : 0 < σ)
    (ŵ : ℕ → (Fin d → ℝ))
    (C_norm : ℝ) (hCn : 0 < C_norm)
    (hw : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∑ i, (ŵ n i)^2 ≤ C_norm) :
    ∃ C' > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      gaussianShiftKL d (ŵ n) σ / n ≤ C' / n := by
  refine' ⟨ C_norm / ( 2 * σ ^ 2 ) + 1, by positivity, _ ⟩;
  filter_upwards [ hw ] with n hn using div_le_div_of_nonneg_right ( by unfold gaussianShiftKL; rw [ div_le_iff₀ <| by positivity ] ; nlinarith [ show 0 ≤ C_norm / ( 2 * σ ^ 2 ) by positivity, show 0 ≤ ∑ i, ŵ n i ^ 2 by exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => sq_nonneg _, mul_div_cancel₀ C_norm <| show ( 2 * σ ^ 2 ) ≠ 0 by positivity ] ) <| Nat.cast_nonneg _;

/-! ## Section 2: Lower Bound -/

/-- Lower bound: the complexity term is Ω(d/n) when the norm is bounded away from zero. -/
theorem pac_bayes_linear_rate_lower
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (τ : ℝ) (hτ : 0 < τ)
    (ŵ : ℕ → (Fin d → ℝ))
    (σ : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hσ_pos : ∀ n, 0 < σ n)

    ∃ c' > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,

  refine' ⟨ C_low / ( 2 * d * τ ^ 2 ), _, _ ⟩;
  · positivity;
  · filter_upwards [ hw_low, hσ_lower, Filter.eventually_gt_atTop 0 ] with n hn hn' hn'';
    gcongr;
    refine' le_trans _ ( le_add_of_nonneg_left _ );
    · rw [ div_mul_eq_mul_div, div_le_div_iff₀ ] <;> nlinarith [ show ( d : ℝ ) ≥ 1 by norm_cast, show ( τ ^ 2 : ℝ ) > 0 by positivity, mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hn ( show ( 0 : ℝ ) ≤ τ ^ 2 by positivity ) ];

/-- The PAC-Bayes complexity term vanishes as n → ∞ under mild assumptions. -/

    (d : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (hτ : 0 < τ)
    (ŵ : ℕ → (Fin d → ℝ))
    (σ : ℕ → ℝ)

    (C_norm C_var : ℝ) (hCn : 0 < C_norm) (hCv : 0 < C_var)
    (hw : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∑ i, (ŵ n i)^2 ≤ C_norm)
    (hσ_upper : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (σ n)^2 ≤ C_var / n)
    (hσ_lower : ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in atTop, 1 / ((m : ℝ))^2 ≤ (σ m)^2) :
    Tendsto (fun (m : ℕ) => gaussianShiftKLFull d (ŵ m) (σ m) τ / (m : ℝ)) atTop (nhds 0) := by
  have h_bound : ∀ᶠ m in atTop, gaussianShiftKLFull d (ŵ m) (σ m) τ ≤ d / 2 * (C_var / (m * τ ^ 2) - 1 - Real.log (1 / (m ^ 2 * τ ^ 2))) + C_norm / (2 * τ ^ 2) := by
    have h_bound : ∀ᶠ m in atTop, gaussianShiftKLFull d (ŵ m) (σ m) τ ≤ d / 2 * (C_var / (m * τ ^ 2) - 1 - Real.log (σ m ^ 2 / τ ^ 2)) + C_norm / (2 * τ ^ 2) := by
      filter_upwards [ hσ_upper, hw ] with n hn hn';
      refine' add_le_add _ _;
      · exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ( by rw [ ← div_div ] ; gcongr ) ( by positivity );
      · gcongr;

    convert div_le_div_of_nonneg_right hm₁ ( Nat.cast_nonneg m ) using 1 ; ring;

        refine h_simplified.congr' ( by filter_upwards [ Filter.eventually_gt_atTop 0 ] with m hm using by rw [ one_div, Real.log_inv, Real.log_mul ( by positivity ) ( by positivity ), Real.log_pow, Real.log_pow ] ; ring );

      simpa using Filter.Tendsto.sub ( h_log_div_m.neg.mul_const 2 ) ( tendsto_const_nhds.mul ( tendsto_inv_atTop_nhds_zero_nat ) |> Filter.Tendsto.mul_const 2 );

/-- Setting σ² = 1/n gives a complexity bounded by d/n times a fixed-rate term. -/
theorem optimal_variance_gives_d_over_n
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (τ : ℝ) (hτ : 0 < τ)
    (w : Fin d → ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C)
    (hw : ∑ i, (w i)^2 ≤ C) :
    gaussianShiftKLFull d w (1 / Real.sqrt (n : ℝ)) τ / (n : ℝ) ≤
      ((d : ℝ) / 2 * (1 / (n * τ^2) - 1 - Real.log (1 / (n * τ^2))) +

  gcongr;

| Library            | #theorems | #anti-gravity | density |
|--------------------|-----------|---------------|---------|
| `discrete n`       | n         | 0             | 0       |
| `star n` (Fin n+1) | n+1       | 1 (the root)  | 1/(n+1) |
| `strongDivLibrary` | 6         | 1 (the root)  | 1/6     |

For every library on `Fin (n+1)`, the top index `Fin.last n` had weight 0 in all

matches `top_weight_zero` and bounds anti-gravity density strictly below 1.

The conservation identity makes ∑ weight equal the edge count of the dependency
DAG; for the `star` family this is the sequence `0,1,2,3,…` (A001477) and offers no
new sequence, so no OEIS submission is warranted. Evidence stage kept intentionally
short per the brief.

# Future Directions

## Weighted and multiplicity-aware dependencies

The present calculus treats `depends u t` as a Boolean: a theorem either relies
on another or it does not. A natural and immediate generalization replaces this
relation with a weight function `w : α → α → Nat`, recording how *many times* `u`
invokes `t`, or how *critically* it does so, and redefines `weight L t` as a sum
of incoming weights rather than a raw in-degree. The key insight is that all of
the averaging machinery — `totalWeight_le_of_all_light` and the
`antigravity_pigeonhole` consequence — is really a statement about sums of
bounded naturals, so it survives the move from cardinalities to weighted sums
almost verbatim, with `Finset.sum_le_sum` doing the same work. **Why now?**
Because the finite, executable scaffolding is already in place and verified;
upgrading the edge type is a localized change that immediately yields strictly
more expressive existence theorems without re-litigating the core combinatorics.

## Transitive load instead of direct in-degree

Direct in-degree undercounts a theorem's true importance: a lemma may be cited by
few results yet underpin enormous reachability cones through them. The next step
is to define a *transitive* weight, the cardinality of `{u | Reaches L u t}`, and
to develop the corresponding anti-gravity notion against this stronger measure.
The key insight is that the reflexive-transitive closure `Reaches`, which we
already use for dependency density, is exactly the object that turns local edges
into global load, so the density layer and the weight layer of the calculus are
two views of the same closure and can be unified. **Why now?** Reachability is
already formalized via `Relation.ReflTransGen` and the `DepDense` API, so the
transitive theory can be built directly atop existing lemmas like
`DepDense_mono` rather than from scratch.

## Algorithmic extraction from real Lean import graphs

Every construct in this development is computable: weights, short sets, and
`antiGravityCandidates` are `Finset.filter` expressions. This opens the door to
running the calculus on the actual dependency graph of Mathlib or another large
formal library, extracting the empirically anti-gravity theorems and comparing
them against human intuition about "foundational" lemmas. The key insight is that
the decidability witness `decidableDepends` carried by every `FiniteLibrary` is
precisely what makes the candidate set executable, so the formal model and a
practical analysis tool are the same artifact rather than two parallel
implementations to keep in sync. **Why now?** Tooling such as `importGraph`
already exposes Lean dependency data, so the missing piece was a verified

# A Finite Dependency Calculus for Theorem Libraries: Anti-Gravity Theorems

## Abstract

We introduce and fully formalize (in Lean 4 / Mathlib) a small, entirely finite
*dependency calculus* for theorem libraries. The objects are **finite
libraries**: finite collections of theorems equipped with a direct-dependency
relation and a proof-length assignment. Within this calculus we isolate the
notion of an **anti-gravity theorem** — a theorem that is simultaneously cheap to
prove yet heavily relied upon — and we prove a pigeonhole existence principle,
basic monotonicity laws, and a reachability/density theory. A canonical
*star library* example exhibits all of these phenomena concretely. Every
definition is executable and every theorem is machine-checked, depending only on
the standard axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.

## 1. Problem statement

Large formal libraries (Mathlib, the AFP, etc.) are dependency graphs: each
theorem is built on others. Two quantities matter for the health of such a
graph. First, the **cost** of a theorem — informally, how long or hard its proof
is. Second, the **load** a theorem bears — how many other results depend on it.
A theorem that is both *cheap* and *load-bearing* is unusually valuable: a small
investment supports a large superstructure. We call such a theorem an
**anti-gravity theorem**, because, despite being "light", it holds up a great
weight.

The questions we formalize are:

1. How should weight (load) and cost be measured in a finite setting?
2. When can we *guarantee* that an anti-gravity theorem exists, purely from
   aggregate statistics of the library?
3. How do anti-gravity theorems interact with *reachability*: can a small set of
   such theorems be "dependency-dense", i.e. reachable from everywhere?

## 2. Finite libraries, weight, anti-gravity, density

Throughout, `α` is a finite type with decidable equality whose elements index
the theorems of the library.

**Finite library.** A `FiniteLibrary α` consists of
* `depends : α → α → Prop`, where `depends u t` reads "theorem `u` depends
  directly on theorem `t`";
* a decidability witness `decidableDepends : DecidableRel depends`, so that all
  derived finsets are executable; and
* `proofLen : α → Nat`, the proof length (cost) of each theorem.

**Weight.** The weight of `t` is its in-degree:
`weight L t = (univ.filter (fun u => L.depends u t)).card`,
the number of theorems that depend directly on `t`.

**Anti-gravity.** Fixing a weight threshold `K` and a length budget `B`,
`AntiGravity L K B t := K ≤ weight L t ∧ L.proofLen t ≤ B`.
Thus `t` is anti-gravity if it is relied upon by at least `K` theorems while
costing at most `B`.

**Short set and candidate set.** `shortSet L B` is the finset of theorems with
`proofLen ≤ B`. `antiGravityCandidates L K B` is the executable finset of all
anti-gravity theorems at thresholds `K, B`. Both are defined by `Finset.filter`
and are therefore computable.

**Reachability and dependency density.** Reachability is the
reflexive-transitive closure of the dependency relation,
`Reaches L := Relation.ReflTransGen L.depends`, oriented so that there is an edge
`u → t` exactly when `u` depends on `t`. A finset `S` is **dependency-dense**,
`DepDense L S`, if every theorem reaches some member of `S` in zero or more
dependency steps: `∀ u, ∃ t ∈ S, Reaches L u t`. Intuitively, `S` is a set of
"foundations" underlying the whole library.

## 3. Theorems and proof sketches

**`weight_le_card`: `weight L t ≤ Fintype.card α`.**
The weight is the cardinality of a filtered subset of `univ`; `Finset.card_filter_le`
bounds it by `univ.card = Fintype.card α`.

**`antigravity_mono`: monotonicity.**
If `K' ≤ K`, `B ≤ B'`, and `AntiGravity L K B t`, then `AntiGravity L K' B' t`.
Unfold the conjunction and chain the two inequalities with transitivity: a
weaker weight demand and a larger budget can only make membership easier.

**`mem_antiGravityCandidates` and `shortSet_mem`: the finsets compute the
predicates.** Both follow by unfolding the `Finset.filter` definitions and
simplifying `Finset.mem_filter` (the `mem_univ` side condition is trivial).

**`totalWeight_le_of_all_light`: an averaging bound.**
Assume `0 < K` and that every short theorem is *light*, `weight L t < K`. Over
naturals, `weight < K` together with `0 < K` gives `weight ≤ K - 1`. Summing
this bound termwise via `Finset.sum_le_sum` and collapsing the constant sum with
`Finset.sum_const` yields
`∑ t ∈ shortSet L B, weight L t ≤ (shortSet L B).card * (K - 1)`.

**`antigravity_pigeonhole`: existence by pigeonhole.**
Assume `0 < K` and `∑ t ∈ shortSet L B, weight L t > (shortSet L B).card * (K-1)`.
We argue by contraposition. If *no* theorem were anti-gravity, then every short
theorem would be light (a short theorem failing anti-gravity must fail the
weight clause), so `totalWeight_le_of_all_light` would bound the total short
weight by `(shortSet L B).card * (K - 1)`, contradicting the hypothesis via
`omega`. Hence some anti-gravity theorem exists. This is the calculus's main
qualitative principle: enough *aggregate* load concentrated on cheap theorems
forces an *individual* cheap-and-load-bearing theorem.

**`DepDense_mono`: density is monotone.**
If `S ⊆ T` and `S` is dependency-dense, so is `T`: a witness reached in `S` is a
witness reached in `T`.

## 4. The star library

The canonical example lives on `Option (Fin n)`: the center is `none` and the
`n` leaves are `some i`. Dependencies are exactly leaf → center
(`depends (some _) none = True`, all others `False`); proof lengths are
`proofLen none = 1` and `proofLen (some _) = 2`.

* **`star_weight_center`: `weight (starLibrary n) starCenter = n`.** The direct
  dependents of `none` are precisely `univ.image some`; by injectivity of `some`
  (`Finset.card_image_of_injective`) this image has cardinality
  `Fintype.card (Fin n) = n`.
* **`star_weight_leaf`: `weight (starLibrary n) (some i) = 0`.** Nothing depends
  on a leaf, so the filtered set is empty.
* **`star_center_antigravity`: `AntiGravity (starLibrary n) n 1 starCenter`.**
  The center has weight `n ≥ n` and proof length `1 ≤ 1`. It is the unique
  anti-gravity theorem at `(K, B) = (n, 1)`: leaves are too long and have weight
  `0`.
* **`star_singleton_depDense`: `{starCenter}` is dependency-dense.** Every leaf
  reaches the center by a single dependency step (`ReflTransGen.single`), and the
  center reaches itself by reflexivity (`ReflTransGen.refl`).
* **`star_candidates_depDense`:** the candidate set at `(K, B) = (n, 1)` is
  dependency-dense, because it contains the center and density is monotone
  (`DepDense_mono`).

The star is the extremal "single foundation" library: a lone cheap theorem
supports everything.

## 5. Significance

The development distills a recurring intuition about formal libraries — that a
few cheap lemmas carry disproportionate structural load — into a precise,
finite, and fully verified calculus. Three features are worth emphasizing.
First, everything is **executable**: weight, short sets, and candidate sets are
`Finset` computations, so the theory could be run directly on a real import
graph. Second, the **pigeonhole principle** turns easily measured aggregate
statistics (total in-degree of short theorems) into a guaranteed structural
conclusion (the existence of an anti-gravity theorem), with no further
assumptions. Third, the **density layer** connects local load (weight) to global
structure (reachability), formalizing the idea of a small foundational core.

## 6. Open questions

* **Weighted dependencies.** Replace the Boolean `depends` with weighted edges
  (multiplicities, usage counts) and recover sharper averaging bounds.
* **Transitive weight.** Measure load by the size of the *reachability* cone
  rather than direct in-degree, and relate the two via the pigeonhole bound.
* **Sharpness.** For which libraries is `antigravity_pigeonhole` tight, and what
  is the minimum size of a dependency-dense anti-gravity set (an extremal /
  covering question)?
* **Extraction.** Can anti-gravity candidates be computed efficiently from the
  actual Lean/Mathlib import graph, and do empirically identified "foundational"
  lemmas coincide with the formal candidates?
* **Dynamics.** As a library grows, how do weight distributions and the
  anti-gravity threshold evolve?

concept.title: The Library of Babel: Combinatorics of the Universal Library
concept.concept_description: Borges' Library of Babel contains every possible 410-page book — approximately 25^{1312000} volumes. The library is finite but vast beyond comprehension. Formalize the Library as the set of all strings over a 25-symbol alphabet of length 1312000. Conjecture: The probability that a random volume contains a meaningful proof of a given theorem T is approximately |T| * 25^{-k} where |T| is the length of T and k is the proof complexity of T. Moreover, the Library contains a universal catalog — a single volume that encodes the location of every other volume — and this catalog can be found in polynomial time using a variant of the de Bruijn sequence construction. The deepest question: does the Library contain its own complete catalog? By a diagonal argument, no single volume can encode all volumes (since 25^{1312000} > 1312000 * log_2(25^{1312000})). But a DISTRIBUTED catalog spanning N volumes can encode the entire Library if N > 25^{1312000} / (1312000 * log_2(25)). Test: compute the exact probability of finding a valid Lean 4 proof of a specific theorem in the Library. Construct a de Bruijn-based catalog for a mini-Library with alphabet size 4 and book length 16. Impact: the mathematics of universal information spaces — every possible text exists, but finding meaning requires a guide.

concept.title: Tropical Cryptography: Min-Plus Encryption with Tropical Matrices
concept.concept_description: Tropical arithmetic (min-plus algebra) replaces + with min and * with +. A tropical matrix A over Z union {infinity} acts on vectors by tropical matrix multiplication: (A tropimes v)_i = min_j (A_{ij} + v_j). Tropical matrices have eigenvalues in the max-plus sense: lambda is a tropical eigenvalue if A tropimes v = lambda + v for some v. Conjecture: tropical matrix multiplication is a one-way function suitable for cryptography. Specifically, the 'tropical discrete logarithm problem' (TDLP) is: given a tropical matrix A and B = A^{otimes k} (tropical matrix power), find k. The tropical matrix power A^{otimes k} is computed in O(n^3 * log(k)) time (by repeated squaring), but recovering k from (A, A^{otimes k}) is hard because the tropical eigenvalues satisfy lambda(A^{otimes k}) = k * lambda(A) (tropical eigenvalues are additive under power), so k = lambda(A^{otimes k}) / lambda(A). But this only works if lambda(A) != 0 (in the tropical sense, lambda(A) != infinity). Conjecture: the tropical Diffie-Hellman key exchange is secure: Alice sends A^{otimes a}, Bob sends A^{otimes b}, and the shared key is A^{otimes ab}. Breaking this requires solving the TDLP, which is believed to be hard for random tropical matrices of size n >= 10. Test: implement the tropical DH key exchange and measure the key generation time vs matrix size. Attempt to break it with known attacks (tropical eigenvalue computation, shortest path algorithms). Impact: tropical arithmetic provides a new foundation for post-quantum cryptography.

concept.lean_guess: Define tropical arithmetic: a oplus b = min(a, b), a otimes b = a + b. Tropical matrix multiplication: (A otimes B)_{ij} = min_k (A_{ik} + B_{kj}). Tropical matrix power: A^{otimes k} = A otimes A otimes ... otimes A (k times). This is equivalent to the k-th power in the min-plus semiring, which is also the all-pairs shortest path matrix for k steps. Tropical eigenvalue: lambda is a tropical eigenvalue of A if there exists v != infinity such that min_j (A_{ij} + v_j) = lambda + v_i for all i. Alice picks a secret a and computes A^{otimes a}. Bob picks a secret b and computes A^{otimes b}. They exchange, and both compute the shared key (A^{otimes a})^{otimes b} = A^{otimes ab} = (A^{otimes b})^{otimes a}. Security: Eve sees A, A^{otimes a}, A^{otimes b} and needs to compute A^{otimes ab}. The tropical eigenvalue gives: lambda(A^{otimes a}) = a * lambda(A), so a = lambda(A^{otimes a}) / lambda(A). This breaks the key exchange! Unless we hide the eigenvalue. Defense: add noise to the matrix before computing the power. A^{otimes k} + noise (in the tropical sense) changes the eigenvalue unpredictably. Conjecture: with noise, the TDLP is hard for n >= 10. Test: implement noisy tropical DH, measure key generation time, attempt to break with eigenvalue attack.

# Compositional Bound: Local-Global Certified Radius for Piecewise-Affine Classifiers

This module formalizes the **compositional certified robustness principle**:
the global certified radius of a piecewise-affine classifier is at least
`min(r_local, r_region)`, where `r_local` is the local affine-margin certificate
radius within a linear region, and `r_region` is the distance to the region boundary.

## Main Results

* `global_radius_ge_min_local_region` — The core lower bound: classification is
  preserved within a ball of radius `min(r_local, r_region)`.

* `exact_global_radius_eq_min` — Equality characterization: under tightness
  conditions on both radii, the global certified radius equals `min(r_local, r_region)`.

* `tropical_compositional_certified_radius` — Full compositional theorem combining
  tropical Lipschitz certificates with region stability.

* `lipschitz_cert_is_global` — The Lipschitz certificate provides a global certificate.

## Mathematical Overview

Inside a fixed linear region of a piecewise-affine (e.g. ReLU) network, each logit
difference `f_y - f_j` is affine. The **local radius** is the largest ball around `x₀`
on which all affine margins stay nonneg while remaining in the same region. The **region
radius** is the distance to the nearest activation-pattern boundary. The compositional
theorem decomposes robustness certification into:
- a **tropical hyperplane arrangement problem** inside a Newton cell,
- a **polyhedral escape problem** to the boundary of a linear region.
-/

/-! ## Section 1: Core Definitions -/

/-- The global certified radius: every point within distance `r` of `x₀` preserves
    class `y` as the argmax of `f`. -/
def GlobalCertified {n k : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, ‖x - x₀‖ < r → ∀ j : Fin k, f x y ≥ f x j

/-- The local certified radius on a region `R`: classification is preserved for
    all points in `R` within distance `r` of `x₀`. -/
def LocalCertified {n k : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k) (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ)) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, x ∈ R → ‖x - x₀‖ < r → ∀ j : Fin k, f x y ≥ f x j

/-- The region radius: the open ball of radius `r` around `x₀` is contained in `R`. -/
def RegionContains {n : ℕ} (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ)) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, ‖x - x₀‖ < r → x ∈ R

/-- A witness for tightness of the local radius: there exists a point on
    the margin boundary at exactly distance `r_local`. -/
def MarginTight {n k : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ j : Fin k, j ≠ y ∧ ∃ x : Fin n → ℝ, ‖x - x₀‖ = r ∧ f x y = f x j

/-- A witness for tightness of the region radius: there exists a boundary
    point at exactly distance `r_region` where crossing leads to class change. -/
def RegionTight {n k : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k) (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ)) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : Fin n → ℝ, ‖x - x₀‖ = r ∧ x ∉ R ∧
    ∃ j : Fin k, j ≠ y ∧ f x j > f x y

/-! ## Section 2: Core Compositional Bound -/

/-
**Main theorem: Compositional certified radius lower bound.**

If `r_local` is a local certified radius within region `R`, and `r_region` ensures
the ball stays inside `R`, then classification is preserved within `min(r_local, r_region)`.

This is the key decomposition: robustness = min(margin safety, region stability).
-/
theorem global_radius_ge_min_local_region
    {n k : ℕ}
    (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ)
    (y : Fin k)
    (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ))
    (r_local r_region : ℝ)
    (hlocal : LocalCertified f x₀ y R r_local)
    (hregion : RegionContains x₀ R r_region) :
    GlobalCertified f x₀ y (min r_local r_region) := by
  grind +locals

/-
Monotonicity: if `GlobalCertified` holds at radius `r`, it holds for any smaller radius.
-/
theorem GlobalCertified.mono {n k : ℕ} {f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ)}
    {x₀ : Fin n → ℝ} {y : Fin k} {r s : ℝ} (h : GlobalCertified f x₀ y r) (hrs : s ≤ r) :
    GlobalCertified f x₀ y s := by
  -- By definition of GlobalCertified, if ‖x - x₀‖ < s ≤ r, then ‖x - x₀‖ < r, so we can apply h.
  intros x hx j; exact h x (by linarith [hx]) j

/-
Monotonicity for local certificates.
-/
theorem LocalCertified.mono {n k : ℕ} {f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ)}
    {x₀ : Fin n → ℝ} {y : Fin k} {R : Set (Fin n → ℝ)} {r s : ℝ}
    (h : LocalCertified f x₀ y R r) (hrs : s ≤ r) :
    LocalCertified f x₀ y R s := by
  exact fun x hx hx' j => h x hx ( lt_of_lt_of_le hx' hrs ) j

/-
A local certificate on the whole space is a global certificate.
-/
theorem LocalCertified.to_global {n k : ℕ} {f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ)}
    {x₀ : Fin n → ℝ} {y : Fin k} {r : ℝ}
    (h : LocalCertified f x₀ y Set.univ r) :
    GlobalCertified f x₀ y r := by
  exact fun x hx j => h x trivial hx j

/-! ## Section 3: Exact Radius Characterization -/

/-
**Equality characterization**: the global certified radius equals
    `min(r_local, r_region)` when the appropriate tightness condition holds.

    The `hglobal_def` hypothesis asserts that no larger radius works as a global
    certificate, making the bound tight. The tightness conditions explain *why*
    the bound is tight: either a margin tie (inside the region) or a region escape
    (at the boundary) is the first obstruction.
-/
theorem exact_global_radius_eq_min
    {n k : ℕ}
    (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ)
    (y : Fin k)
    (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ))
    (r_local r_region : ℝ)
    (hr_local_pos : r_local > 0)
    (hr_region_pos : r_region > 0)
    (hlocal : LocalCertified f x₀ y R r_local)
    (hregion : RegionContains x₀ R r_region)
    (htight_local : r_local ≤ r_region → MarginTight f x₀ y r_local)
    (htight_region : r_region ≤ r_local → RegionTight f x₀ y R r_region)
    (hglobal_def : ∀ r, GlobalCertified f x₀ y r → r ≤ min r_local r_region) :
    ∀ r, GlobalCertified f x₀ y r ↔ r ≤ min r_local r_region := by
  refine' fun r => ⟨ hglobal_def r, fun hr => _ ⟩;
  exact GlobalCertified.mono ( global_radius_ge_min_local_region f x₀ y R r_local r_region hlocal hregion ) hr

/-! ## Section 4: Tropical Lipschitz Local Certificate -/

/-
**Bridge to tropical spectral bounds**: If the network has Lipschitz constant
    `K` and tropical degree `d`, then the pairwise tropical certificate radius
    provides a local certificate on any region.
-/
theorem tropical_local_certificate
    {n k : ℕ}
    (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k)
    (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ))
    (K : ℝ≥0) (hK : 0 < K)
    (hlip : ∀ j, LipschitzWith K (fun x => f x j))
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
    (hcorrect : ∀ j, j ≠ y → f x₀ y > f x₀ j)
    (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ R)
    (r : ℝ) (hr : r > 0)
    (hr_bound : ∀ j, j ≠ y → r ≤ (f x₀ y - f x₀ j) / (2 * K * d)) :
    LocalCertified f x₀ y R r := by
  intro x hx hx' j; by_cases hj : j = y <;> simp_all +decide [ div_le_iff₀ ] ;
  -- Apply the Lipschitz property to get the bounds on the differences.
  have h_lip : ‖f x y - f x₀ y‖ ≤ K * ‖x - x₀‖ ∧ ‖f x j - f x₀ j‖ ≤ K * ‖x - x₀‖ := by
    exact ⟨ by simpa using hlip y |>.dist_le_mul x x₀, by simpa using hlip j |>.dist_le_mul x x₀ ⟩;
  have := hr_bound j hj;
  rw [ le_div_iff₀ ] at this <;> norm_num at *;
  · nlinarith [ abs_le.mp h_lip.1, abs_le.mp h_lip.2, show ( d : ℝ ) ≥ 1 by norm_cast, show ( K : ℝ ) > 0 by positivity, mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ( show ( d : ℝ ) ≥ 1 by norm_cast ) ( show ( K : ℝ ) ≥ 0 by positivity ) ];
  · positivity

/-
**Full compositional theorem with tropical certificates.**

Combines `tropical_local_certificate` with the region containment
to get a global certified radius from tropical spectral data.
-/
theorem tropical_compositional_certified_radius
    {n k : ℕ}
    (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k)
    (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ))
    (K : ℝ≥0) (hK : 0 < K)
    (hlip : ∀ j, LipschitzWith K (fun x => f x j))
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
    (hcorrect : ∀ j, j ≠ y → f x₀ y > f x₀ j)
    (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ R)
    (r_local : ℝ) (hr_local : r_local > 0)
    (hr_local_bound : ∀ j, j ≠ y → r_local ≤ (f x₀ y - f x₀ j) / (2 * K * d))
    (r_region : ℝ)
    (hregion : RegionContains x₀ R r_region) :
    GlobalCertified f x₀ y (min r_local r_region) := by

/-! ## Section 5: Lipschitz Global Certificate -/

/-
The Lipschitz certificate: within radius `gap / (2K)` for each competing class,

-/
